reason: Reveal B prioritizes readable prediction content and keeps Share visible at 200%. History A preserves both question and forecast with readable dates. Error A brings the entire recovery choice set into the enlarged viewport. Reveal A is the stronger ceremonial alternative; History B becomes attractive with frequent same-day entries; Error C adds useful question context. None demonstrates the required browser A>=9 and F>=9 across every screen and component.
limitations: Independent read-only assessment of the six attached sheets and supplied evidence descriptions only. No files, prior ratings, other graders or runtime tools were consulted.

Each screen score combines normal and 200% views. Component tuples use [hierarchy, typography/spacing, surfaces/color, clarity, feedback/recovery, accessibility]. X denotes accessibility; null denotes an inapplicable dimension or an undemonstrated component interaction.

Numeric feedback grades assess visible qualification, state, reassurance and recovery guidance; supplied baseline runtime evidence is identified where used. Prototype study-status announcements do not prove sharing, reminders, history opening or recovery.

Grades and calculated overall scores are provisional. Physical/native evidence is recorded as missing rather than used as a blanket score deduction. Browser evidence also does not establish target sizes, focus behavior, keyboard operation, screen-reader semantics or measured contrast for these prototypes.

Viewport boundaries do not prove content loss or unreachable controls. Baseline reveal fragmentation, baseline History month splitting and Error B's partially displayed enlarged input are distinct visible readability weaknesses.
No whole-screen hard-gate failure is established by these sheets. Offscreen content and the input's internal scrolling require direct checks before stronger accessibility conclusions.
Prototype orb motion, loading, selected states, transitions, actual recovery and representative novice outcomes remain unverified. Baseline proof does not transfer to alternatives.
Synthetic fixture wording and repeated questions are study artifacts. History alternatives omit the baseline navigation; their integration into the product and return paths are not demonstrated.
